items.title: Alphabet’s Investment Write-Down Drove the Earnings Miss, Not the Business – Goldman Sachs Says Buy
items.summary: Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) just ended a 12-quarter run, and investors sold hard. Shares traded at $285.31 this morning, down 12.18% in the session. Business Insider reported that the drop erased a huge amount of market value. The miss looks worse than the business, though, and Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) still rates the stock a Buy […]

analysis.summary: Alphabet missed earnings due to an $8.7 billion investment write‑down, but revenue grew 24.6% YoY and AI‑driven cloud is outpacing rivals, prompting Goldman Sachs to keep a Buy rating despite a lower price target.
analysis.catalyst: Alphabet’s Q2 earnings miss driven by a one‑time investment write‑down, while AI‑powered cloud growth and strong search query growth signal a longer‑term upside
analysis.horizon: 4-6 weeks, until the post‑earnings price correction stabilizes and the next quarterly guidance is released
analysis.explanation: Alphabet’s earnings fell short because of a large, non‑recurring write‑down, not because the core business is weakening. Revenue grew nearly 25% and Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, beating both Azure and AWS growth rates, which shows the AI infrastructure tailwind is material. Goldman Sachs still rates the stock a Buy and only trimmed its target, implying the market is over‑penalizing the miss. Over the next month‑plus, the share price should rebound as investors re‑price the underlying growth story and the write‑down impact fades. A long position in GOOGL captures that upside while avoiding the noise of short‑term volatility.
rationale: Core earnings miss is accounting‑driven, not operational
AI‑driven cloud growth outpaces peers, supporting multi‑year revenue expansion
Goldman maintains Buy, indicating market undervaluation
analysis.risk: If AI spending slows or the free‑cash‑flow gap widens, the stock could stay depressed despite the write‑down being one‑off

items.title: Archer-Daniels-Midland: Caution Warranted Amid Recent Financial Volatility (Earnings Preview)

analysis.summary: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM) is flagged as a hold because recent cash‑flow volatility and a relatively high valuation raise concerns despite a strong turnaround in its Ag Services and Oilseeds segment.
analysis.catalyst: Upcoming Q3 2026 earnings on Nov 3 that could confirm whether profit growth sustains the turnaround
analysis.horizon: 3‑4 weeks, exiting after the Q3 earnings release if results miss guidance or volatility persists
analysis.explanation: The analyst notes that ADM’s earnings have improved thanks to higher oilseed prices and supportive policies, but cash‑flow volatility remains a red flag and the stock trades at a premium to peers. With the next earnings report only a week away, the market will price in whether the turnaround is durable. A negative FinBERT sentiment and the "caution warranted" tone suggest investors are uneasy. By shorting ADM now we can capture a potential downside if earnings miss or volatility spikes, and we can close the position quickly after the earnings announcement, avoiding longer‑term exposure to commodity price swings. This trade is more direct than buying a broader agriculture ETF, which would dilute the specific risk we’re targeting.
rationale: High valuation relative to peers despite volatile cash flow
Earnings catalyst on Nov 3 could confirm or refute the sustainability of the turnaround
Negative sentiment and analyst hold rating imply downside risk
analysis.risk: If ADM’s earnings beat expectations and cash‑flow volatility eases, the stock could rally, eroding the short position.
